sections.md: The Decision's single operative article instructs only the central administrator: "the central administrator of the European Union Transaction Log is instructed to enter the corrected national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).* No addressee clause naming Member States, economic operators, or private parties was located in the captured text; the workspace sits entirely outside the Decision's operative scope.

The corrections addressed by this Decision are installation-level data fixes: for example, "Sweden notified corrections to its national allocation table by letter dated 22 November 2021," concerning "reported values for electricity consumption that are used for calculating the electricity" component of free allocation, and Finland "corrected the reported heat values and therefore the historical activity levels" after several installations "reported wrong heat balance between eligible and non-eligible heat for free allocation." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).* These are registry-accuracy corrections to the transitional free-allocation calculation for named installations, not new obligations.

*Specific effective date, compliance deadline, and penalty provision not available from primary sources as of the export date: the captured text is a single-article administrative instruction to the Central Administrator, states no entry-into-force clause, no deadline binding an external party, and no penalty or sanction provision.*

"Member States submitted to the Commission the list of installations under their territory pursuant to Article 11(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council," the directive establishing the EU ETS. The Decision instructs entry into the Union Transaction Log of "corrected national allocation tables... for the transitional free allocation of emission allowances for the period from 2021 to 2025." *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).* This is a technical, administrative EU ETS registry correction affecting the free-allowance entitlement of specific stationary industrial installations in the ten named Member States, not an obligation reaching the workspace directly; it belongs to the background EU ETS allocation machinery that shapes the carbon-cost environment those installations, and any freight that serves them, operate in.

Registration and reporting under the EU ETS free-allocation regime runs through the national allocation tables the ten Member States submitted under Directive 2003/87/EC Article 11(1); this Decision is the Commission's instruction to record the corrected versions of those tables, not a new filing requirement. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

- Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 (2022/C 77/02), European Commission, OJ C 77/19, published 2022 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02)

- 17 December 2021: Commission adopts the Decision instructing entry of the corrected national allocation tables ("Done at Brussels, 17 December 2021"). In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*
- 22 November 2021: Sweden notifies its national allocation table corrections by letter, addressed by this Decision. In force as of the export date. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

No workspace-facing operational system build is indicated by this Decision's text; the corrections apply to the free-allocation calculations of named EU ETS installations administered by the ten Member States and the Commission. *No operational system requirement identified for the workspace as of the export date.*

This document analyzes a Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 (2022/C 77/02) instructing the central administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter corrected national allocation tables of free EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) allowances for ten Member States, "Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden," into the log. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

**MONITORING.** No workspace-facing deadline or obligation is stated in this Decision's own text; the corrective action runs between the Commission, the named Member States, and the central administrator of the registry. *Operational implication:* for workspaces with cargo verticals touching EU ETS-covered industrial installations (e.g., high-value automotive manufacturing supply chains in the affected Member States), this correction has no direct compliance step for the forwarder, but it is one input into the free-allocation baseline those installations' own carbon cost exposure is measured against. *Source: Commission Decision of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log, European Commission, OJ C 77/19, 2022/C 77/02. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32022D0217(02).*

pool.text: C_2022077EN.01001901.xml 17.2.2022 EN Official Journal of the European Union C 77/19 COMMISSION DECISION of 17 December 2021 instructing the Central Administrator of the European Union Transaction Log to enter the national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden into the European Union Transaction Log 2022/C 77/02 THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION, Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Having regard to Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/1122 of 12 March 2019 supplementing Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the functioning of the Union Registry ( 1 ) , and in particular Article 46(2) thereof, Whereas: (1) Member States submitted to the Commission the list of installations under their territory pursuant to Article 11(1) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 2 ) . (2) In accordance with Article 2 of Commission Decision (EU) 2021/355 ( 3 ) , the Commission raised no objections to the lists of installations covered by Directive 2003/87/EC as submitted by Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Estonia, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Croatia, Italy, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Hungary, the Netherlands, Austria, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Finland and Sweden, except as set out in Article 1 and Annexes of that Decision. (3) Member States determined and notified the preliminary annual amounts of free allowances per installation using the revised benchmark values determined in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/447 ( 4 ) , pursuant to Article 14(5) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 ( 5 ) . (4) In Article 1 of Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/927 ( 6 ) , it was determined that no adjustment needs to be applied to the preliminary annual amounts of free allowances pursuant to Article 10a(5) of Directive 2003/87/EC, as demand did not exceed the maximum amount. (5) Belgium notified changes to its national allocation table, by letter dated 27 October 2021. The changes concerned installations BE-215020, BE-204193, BE-215022, BE-215200, BE-215240, BE-276, BE-215060 and BE-215220 that were included in the initial national allocation table with their provisional identification numbers of the registry account. Belgium reported the new permanent numbers. Moreover, Belgium corrected the amount of heat produced under carbon leakage risk of installation BE-256 and therefore, the initial final amount of free allowances was corrected. (6) Germany notified changes to its national allocation table, by letter dated 18 November 2021. Installation DE-79 corrected the annual activity levels of the grey cement clinker sub-installation and the calculated historical activity level. The heat balance in installation DE-531 was corrected as more heat imported from installation that was not under emissions trading system (ETS) was consumed for the product benchmark sub-installation. Also, the heat balance in installation DE-950 was corrected as part of the heat was not reported as export to ETS installation. The operators of installations DE-1480 and DE-206010 renounced their application for free emissions allowances. Installation DE-new-14611-0017 was introduced in the system after the split of incumbent installation DE-205246 into two installations. The split occurred after the submission of German national implementation measures on 31 September 2019 and was not reported in the national allocation table, which should be corrected accordingly. (7) Greece notified a correction in its national allocation table concerning installation GR-203127, by letter dated 15 October 2021. Installation GR-203073 was merged with installation GR-203127, however, only data from the first installation was reported in the final national implementation measures and consequently the final annual amount of emissions allowances was not correct. Greece corrected its national allocation table by updating the data concerning the new merged installation. (8) Croatia notified a correction in its national allocation table by letter dated 4 October 2021. Installation HR-205907 was included by mistake in the national allocation table as it was excluded from ETS pursuant to Article 27. (9) Latvia notified corrections in its national allocation table concerning the registry identification number of installations LV-204013, LV-114 and LV-206234, by letter dated 10 November 2021. (10) Hungary notified corrections in its national allocation table that occurred because it was not in line with the submission of the final national implementation measures by mistake. The national allocation table was replaced with the correct one. Hungary notified the necessary changes by letter dated 15 November 2021. (11) The Netherlands notified a correction in its national allocation table by letter dated 5 November 2021. The change concerned installation NL-99. The Netherlands identified errors in the calculation of the historical activity level of the refinery products sub-installation and in particular, the CO 2 weighted tonnes. (12) Poland notified a correction in its national allocation table by letter dated 24 November 2021, concerning installation PL-208182. Poland corrected the split of heat produced into carbon leakage risk and non-carbon leakage risk sub-installations. (13) Finland notified corrections to its national allocation table by letter dated 26 November 2021. Installations FI-12, FI- 207707, FI-236, FI-239, FI-398, FI-450, FI-457, FI-458, FI-477, FI-632, FI-650 reported wrong heat balance between eligible and non-eligible heat for free allocation. Finland corrected the reported heat values and therefore the historical activity levels. (14) Sweden notified corrections to its national allocation table by letter dated 22 November 2021. The corrections regarding installation SE-350 concern reported values for electricity consumption that are used for calculating the electricity exchange factor. The corrections regarding installation SE-426 concern errors in determination of the CWT values for propylene production. As regards installation SE-428, the operator did not report the uncoated carton board in units of adt (6 % water content) but instead they reported the uncoated carton board with a humidity of 1,2 to 1,4 %. As regards installation SE-812, the reported status regarding electricity production was erroneously reported as ‘False’ while it should be ‘True’. (15) The notified national allocation tables are in conformity with Directive 2003/87/EC and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 and Decision (EU) 2021/355, HAS DECIDED AS FOLLOWS: Single article The central administrator of the European Union Transaction Log is instructed to enter the corrected national allocation tables of Belgium, Germany, Greece, Croatia, Latvia, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Finland and Sweden, with the final annual amounts for the transitional free allocation of emission allowances for the period from 2021 to 2025, as set out in the Annex, into the European Union Transaction Log. Done at Brussels, 17 December 2021. For the Commission Frans TIMMERMANS Executive Vice-President ( 1 ) OJ L 177, 2.7.2019, p. 3 . ( 2 ) Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 October 2003 establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Community and amending Council Directive 96/61/EC ( OJ L 275, 25.10.2003, p. 32 ). ( 3 ) Commission Decision (EU) 2021/355 of 25 February 2021 concerning national implementation measures for the transitional free allocation of greenhouse gas emission allowances in accordance with Article 11(3) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( OJ L 68, 26.2.2021, p. 221 ). ( 4 ) Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/447 of 12 March 2021 determining revised benchmark values for free allocation of emission allowances for the period from 2021 to 2025 pursuant to Article 10a(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( OJ L 87, 15.3.2021, p. 29 ). ( 5 ) Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 of 19 December 2018 determining transitional Union-wide rules for harmonised free allocation of emission allowances pursuant to Article 10a of Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( OJ L 59, 27.2.2019, p. 8 ). ( 6 ) Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/927 of 31 May 2021 determining the uniform cross-sectoral correction factor for the adjustment of free allocations of emission allowances for the period 2021 to 2025 ( OJ L 203, 9.6.2021, p. 14 ). sections.md: - Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register document 2026-13092, June 29 2026 (Tier 1, primary binding text). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks

For workspaces whose clients are farm producers, aggregators, or intermediary entities in the reduced-CI feedstock chain: (1) confirm the client's Biofuel Feedstock Report and supporting nutrient-management and manure-application records are retained for the 5-year window this rule sets, and (2) confirm any third-party verifier engagement covers all sustainability certification programs the client participates in, to avoid double-counted GHG benefit claims. *Operational implication:* neither requirement creates a direct forwarding-side system build, since the recordkeeping duty sits with the producer, aggregator, or intermediary, not the carrier or forwarder. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.

The rule's obligations attach to farm producers, the first point of aggregation, and intermediary entities in the reduced-CI feedstock supply chain, not to carriers or forwarders. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any workspace activity (e.g., commissioning aggregation, warehousing, or onward distribution of reduced-CI feedstock crop on behalf of a client) brings the workspace within the "first point of aggregation" or "intermediary entities" language the rule uses for its attestation and recordkeeping duties. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.

The rule "supports the quantification, reporting, and verification of greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction benefits resulting from implementation of low-carbon practices in the production of commodities that are used as biofuel feedstocks in the context of environmental services markets." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks. It applies directly to farm producers of covered feedstock crops (field corn, soybeans, sorghum, spring canola) and to the first point of aggregation and intermediary entities handling reduced-carbon-intensity (reduced-CI) crop. For workspaces that arrange transport or forwarding for agricultural biofuel feedstocks, or that serve clients participating in reduced-CI feedstock or sustainable aviation fuel supply chains, this rule sets the federal documentation and carbon-intensity attestation regime those upstream counterparties must meet. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace itself, as a freight forwarder rather than a farm producer, aggregator, or intermediary entity, falls within any duty-holder class this rule defines.

**MONITORING.** Assess whether any current or prospective client shipping biofuel feedstock crops or reduced-CI processed product relies on USDA FD-CIC certification, since the rule "specifically applies to the production of low- carbon biofuel feedstocks for liquid transportation fuels, which presents a clear environmental services market." *Operational implication:* a forwarder handling reduced-CI feedstock cargo may be asked by shippers to confirm chain-of-custody documentation aligns with the attestation records this rule requires further upstream, even though the forwarder itself is not a named duty-holder in the text. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.

The rule does not establish a jurisdictional or producer registration scheme; it operates through the Biofuel Feedstock Report and third-party verification process described above rather than a standing agency registration. *Specific registration or filing deadline not available from primary sources as of the export date.*

**Carbon-intensity quantification and attestation.** Farm producers document field- or management-unit-level carbon intensity using USDA FD-CIC, which "estimates feedstock CIs based on user location, user supplied nutrient management information, and, if applicable, the impact of one or more low-carbon practices." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.

**MONITORING. Recordkeeping and attestation under penalty of perjury.** The Biofuel Feedstock Report submitted by farm producers, and the attestations required of the first point of aggregation and intermediary entities, must be signed under penalty of perjury: the report must "begin with a statement that the undersigned farm producer certifies the following under penalties of perjury." *Operational implication:* this is a federal false-statement liability mechanism, not a stated civil fine amount; a workspace advising a client on documentation integrity for reduced-CI cargo should treat the attestation as carrying personal legal exposure for the signer, distinct from any commercial penalty. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.

**Third-party verification.** Entities "participating in multiple sustainability certification programs must now provide a third-party verifier with documentation related to their participation in those programs... in order to ensure that environmental benefits (i.e., GHG emissions reductions) are not accounted for in multiple programs." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.

**Record retention.** Nutrient-management records supporting a claimed low-carbon practice "must be kept for 5 years." *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.

- July 29, 2026: rule effective ("DATES: Effective date: July 29, 2026."). In force as of the export date. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.
- The interim rule preceding this final rule took public comment for 60 days, ending March 18, 2025, and USDA received 114 comments before finalizing the changes reflected in this rule. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.

This document analyzes the USDA final rule "Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks" (7 CFR part 2100), published as Federal Register document 2026-13092 on June 29, 2026, and effective July 29, 2026. The rule finalizes the USDA Feedstock Carbon Intensity Calculator (USDA FD-CIC), which quantifies, reports on, and verifies greenhouse gas reduction benefits from low-carbon agricultural practices used to produce biofuel feedstock crops. *Source: Technical Guidelines for the Production of Regenerative Agricultural Biofuel Feedstocks, USDA, Federal Register 2026-13092, June 29 2026. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/06/29/2026-13092/technical-guidelines-for-the-production-of-regenerative-agricultural-biofuel-feedstocks.
